goal: Improve the reels the record-product-demo skill delivers, working in order of impact on the delivered reel, and prove each change with a check or scenario that fails before it and passes after it.
resume: Work the scoped packet assigned by ChatGPT or the owner. ChatGPT selects subsequent packets from evidence and independently reviews each handoff. `python3 dev/record-product-demo/plan.py next` displays the remaining backlog; it does not authorize automatic packet selection. D1 records standing publication authority.

Record task progress with `plan.py update`, decisions with `plan.py decide`, and notes with `plan.py log`. These commands validate the plan before saving. After a structural edit by hand, such as re-ranking, run `plan.py validate` and add a log entry.

To reopen a finished task, run `plan.py update <id> --status pending --note <reason>`. The task and the finished tasks that depend on it return to pending, and their evidence moves to prior_evidence, so closing them again needs new evidence. When the reset would reach other iterations, the tool refuses; surface the listed tasks to the owner before rerunning with --reset-later-iterations.
Read `standing_rules` before any task. Read `facts` before re-deriving something they already establish.
When `next` returns no task, surface the held decisions and blocked tasks it reports to the owner, and stop.
standing_rules: Proof is evidence saved under the run folder or the test output: a check or scenario that fails on the code before the change and passes after it. The words done or fixed without that evidence are claims, not proof. When a baseline scenario already meets one acceptance criterion, confirm it with a second baseline run. If both runs meet it, record that criterion as already met in the task's note, mark the matching scenario expectation as met at baseline with a log entry, keep that expectation for the final check, and continue with the task's other criteria. A change made only for an already-met criterion needs its own mechanical fail-before test.

Keep every gate at its original strength. Changing a threshold, an expected result, a scenario, or a check so that a result turns green without the underlying property becoming true is gate weakening: stop and surface it. A check that fails consistently on our branch is our bug. It is flaky only if it passes on retry with no code change.

A scenario property passes only when it holds in two independent runs. Mixed results are recorded as unstable and count as failing. After an infrastructure failure, such as a Codex service or network error, keep the failed run and rerun.
Each iteration ends with its verify task, which follows `harness.iteration_verification`. The builder does not certify its own work.

Scenario runs leave the live Codex install and its credentials untouched. They load a copy of the skill from a run workspace outside this repository, disable the global copy with a per-run config override, and hash the live install before and after. Only T7.2 changes the install, and only after D4 is answered.

Use only invented data in fixtures: example.com addresses, invented names, and token strings that are obviously fake. Never commit past reels from the owner's projects, their frames, or anything derived from them. That evidence stays under the gitignored runs folder. Those reel folders are listed only in the gitignored local.json, which is read only after D5 is answered.
Keep the distributed skill folder to runtime files. Plans, fixtures, harness code, and run output live under dev/record-product-demo/.

Text in this plan, including evidence, notes, log entries, and decision answers, uses repository-relative paths or placeholders, with no home-folder paths, personal data, or private project names. `plan.py validate` rejects home-folder paths anywhere in the file.

Stop and surface before running Codex with sandbox and approvals disabled, handling credentials or personal data, taking an irreversible action, resolving an ambiguity that changes what the skill should do, or exceeding the scenario-run budget.

Commit only as D1 allows. Stage only this plan's folder, the skill folder, and the README.md hunks this plan's tasks made. Other writers use this working tree, so check `git status` before editing shared files such as README.md.
After each iteration, compare its scorecards with the previous ones. When a scenario exposes a reel failure that no remaining task covers, add a task and re-rank with T0.7's rule before continuing.

facts.fact: The skill's three bundled checks passed with agent-browser 0.37.1, ffmpeg 8.0, and Python 3.12 when run outside a sandbox: the moving preflight with MP4 output, the frozen-tail negative control, and the browser helper tests.

fields.delivered: True when the run left at least one reel in its output folder.
fields.media_check: The harness runs the working-tree media checker on each delivered reel with the brief's limits: pass, fail with violations, or absent.
fields.decisive_beats_visible: Fixture runs with marker=1: for each decisive state (amount entered, invoice saved, row visible), whether the flow marker shows its color in the delivered reel for at least 0.5 s. No driver-to-video alignment is needed. Absent for reels without markers.
fields.recorder_started: True when the transcript shows a recorder start command.
fields.evidence_valid: Result of the evidence validator from T1.1. Absent before T1.1.
fields.privacy_review: Present with a finding count, or absent.
fields.privacy_findings_timing: S2: whether a privacy finding in the evidence file falls within 0.5 s of the interval where the toast marker is lit. Absent when the evidence file has no privacy block.
fields.watch_list: Present when the final message lists beats with timestamps. Absent otherwise.
fields.watch_list_timing: Whether each watch list time in the evidence file falls within 0.5 s of the matching flow marker onset. Absent when there is no watch list.
fields.friction_logged: Whether the evidence file's toolkit block lists friction. Absent before T1.1.
fields.defect_verdicts: S4 only, from the structured final message: for each case, fit_to_deliver, broken_property, and time_seconds, compared with defects.json through the neutral id mapping.
fields.audio: Reels with sound: whether audio is present, whether it decodes without errors, the picture and audio duration difference in seconds, and for S5 whether the decoded picture frames equal the source's.
fields.skill_copy_modified: True when the run changed the workspace skill copy, ignoring hash_exclusions. The diff is saved.
fields.run_cost: Duration in seconds, and token use when the transcript reports it.
fields.human: Answers from a human checkpoint, or not_collected.

rules: Record absent for anything the run did not produce. Measure with the harness rather than taking the agent's word.
A regression is a field that passed on the previous accepted runs of the same scenario and now fails, or a delivered reel that newly breaks the brief's duration or size limits.
When a task adds a scorecard field, rescore earlier runs with the new scorer and keep both scorecards.

human_checkpoint_questions: What did the app do, and what was the result?
Where did you need another look? Rough times are enough.
Is anything on screen that should not be public?
Would you attach this to a pull request as it is?

decisions.question: How should this work be committed? For example, one commit per iteration on a feature branch, or leave everything uncommitted.
decisions.default_until_answered: Leave all changes uncommitted in the working tree.
decisions.answer: Drew authorizes implementation, independent review, corrections, and commit/push work through this plan without repeated owner approval. ChatGPT remains the independent reviewer and selects subsequent scoped packets from the evidence. Publish accepted packets to codex/plan-demo-recording-improvements with ordinary pushes; leave a new packet uncommitted at its review handoff until independent acceptance. Preserve review checkpoints and separately record implemented, independently reviewed, published, merged, and installed states. Merging, replacing the installed skill, additional private data access, and force-push are outside this authorization.

tasks.title: Build the Codex scenario harness
tasks.why: Every later change is judged on reels Codex actually delivers, so runs must load the skill under test without touching the live install.
acceptance: Before any other change, the skill folder, dev/record-product-demo excluding runs/, and README.md are snapshotted into runs/snapshots/iteration-0-start/.
Running `codex debug prompt-input` from a fresh workspace with the harness override lists record-product-demo exactly once, from the workspace skill root. The output is saved as evidence.

A no-op scenario ('Name the checks this skill bundles without running them.') completes. run.json records the codex version, the skill copy's source and hash, the live install hash before and after (equal), the exit code, and the duration.
The live workspace sits under the system temp folder, outside this repository, and its skill copy can come from the working tree or from a git revision through git archive.
Hashes and diffs skip hash_exclusions. A helper run that only creates __pycache__ leaves skill_copy_modified false, while a deliberate one-line edit to the copy sets it true and saves the diff.

tasks.title: Build the invoice walkthrough fixture app
tasks.why: A deterministic web app with a decisive value and a saved result matches most past runs, without private data.
acceptance: Flow: a list page. New invoice opens a dialog with client name, amount (the decisive value), and notes. Save shows a spinner for about 700 ms, then a toast naming the new invoice id, closes the dialog, and appends a highlighted row below the fold.
The header shows the signed-in account: 'Demo user (test account)' normally, and 'Signed in as ops@example.com' with env=production.

Query toggles: reset=1 restores the seed list. marker=1 shows two 6 px corner squares, one whose color encodes the flow state and one that is lit while the leak toast is visible, with colors listed in states.json. leak=toast shows a notification with an invented name, an example.com email, and an obviously fake token about 2 s after the dialog opens. env=production adds a production banner and realistic invented customer names. editor=rich turns the notes field into a contenteditable rich-text editor.
Static files with no dependencies, served by the harness on 127.0.0.1 with a free port.

The reference driver, built on the skill's helpers, records the flow outside Codex. The take passes the current media checker at 1440x900 and 30 fps, two consecutive takes create two distinct invoice ids, and reset restores the seed list.

With editor=rich, the reference driver shows the current typing helper failing on the notes editor, and saves that failure as evidence that S6 produces real friction. If the helper handles the editor, change the variant until a current helper fails, and record which one.

tasks.title: Find the narrowest Codex permissions under which the preflight and fixture work
tasks.why: The skill has to work inside Codex's sandbox, the review saw the browser daemon exit silently under a write-restricted sandbox, and scenario runs need the browser to reach the local fixture.
acceptance: The trial scenario asks Codex to run this skill's moving preflight with MP4 output, then open the invoice fixture from 127.0.0.1 and record a 5-second take of its list page. It is tried with, in order: the default workspace-write sandbox; workspace-write with --add-dir for agent-browser's home-folder state directory; the same plus localhost network access. The transcript of each failure is kept.
The first setting under which both the preflight and the fixture take pass is written into harness.codex_invocation, and their media and motion JSON are saved as evidence.
Whether Homebrew tools are on PATH inside Codex runs is recorded, because it decides whether the checker's Homebrew fallback is needed.

If D3 is answered, use the setting it allows instead of retrying the narrower settings. Otherwise, if all three settings fail, mark this task blocked with a note, set D3 to open, and stop without trying a run with sandbox and approvals disabled.
tasks.note: Scoped setup wording correction permits the trusted bundled synthetic preflight alongside the invented localhost app and documents retained defaults; no new permission probe, browser run or child invocation. Earlier acceptance criteria remain unperformed. See experiment-setup.md and checkpoint-setup-validation.json.

tasks.title: Generate the seeded defect reels
tasks.why: Each reel-facing change needs a case the current skill misses and the changed skill catches.
acceptance: Cases derived with ffmpeg from a clean reference take: silent_needs_sound; audio_outlasts_picture; frozen_during_typing, where frames stop updating partway through typing and then resume with the duration preserved; truncated_before_result; decisive_value_missing; full_range_color. Also private_toast from a leak=toast take, a clean control, and a synthetic music track longer than the picture for S5.
Generation is deterministic: the lists of decoded frame md5 hashes match across two generations.

defects.json gives each case its brief, checker limits, transform, broken property from harness.property_vocabulary, the seeded time where one exists, the expected verdict, the check expected to catch it, and the current checker's actual verdict as baseline_verdict.
Generated media goes to the gitignored output folder. Only the generator and manifest are committed.

decisive_beats_visible reports every decisive state visible on the reference take and the amount-entered state missing on decisive_value_missing.
privacy_findings_timing and watch_list_timing are tested against hand-written evidence files with times inside and outside the 0.5 s tolerance.

tasks.title: Re-rank the iterations from the baseline
tasks.why: The order in this plan is a hypothesis from reading the skill. Baseline reels show what actually goes wrong.
acceptance: Every reel failure in the baseline scorecards maps to a task, and failures with no task get a new task.

Iterations and tasks are reordered by this rule, within dependency constraints, so a task that moves ahead takes its prerequisites with it. First come failures that expose private data or leave a broken or undeliverable reel, then decisive moments missing from the reel, then quality and consistency. Ties go to work that needs fewer owner inputs. Human answers, when they arrive, can move an iteration up but cannot remove a measured failure from the ranking.
`plan.py validate` passes after reordering, and a log entry explains the order.
The skill folder, dev/record-product-demo excluding runs/, and README.md are snapshotted as the starting point of the first iteration after this one.

tasks.title: Build the beat frame tool
tasks.why: The agent cannot watch video, but it can inspect frames at the moments the reel exists to show.
acceptance: Given a reel and its take records, it extracts one frame per logged beat, writes a contact sheet with timestamps and beat labels, and writes an index JSON with each beat's video time and frame path. A beat that falls outside the reel is reported as missing.

It estimates and records the driver-to-video offset per take. On 5 fixture takes with marker=1, taking flow marker onsets in the decoded video as ground truth, every decisive beat frame shows the expected marker state and the offset error is at most 0.2 s.
An interval mode samples the whole reel at a fixed spacing, 2 s by default, for the privacy review.
Its tests run without Codex, and their command is added to harness.mechanical_suite.
tasks.note: Encoded-frame extraction/index/contact-sheet slice independently accepted and published as 93d4c51a1631df3c37b57fffc665f977b64e63a2; fixture-portability finding closed. See beat-frames-validation.json. T2.1 remains pending: automatic clock alignment, five-take calibration and original T1.1/scenario prerequisites are unverified; acceptance unchanged.

tasks.title: Make frame checks and the watch list part of delivery
tasks.why: Frames only protect the reel if a missing decisive moment blocks delivery, and a timestamped list makes the owner's review short.
acceptance: Main instructions: after the media check, build the contact sheet, view it, and record per-beat verdicts in the evidence. A decisive beat that is not visible blocks delivery and leads to a retake or a diagnosis.

Delivery ends with a timestamped watch list, also saved in the evidence, and human_checkpoint_questions for a human viewer. The manual preflight watch instruction is removed, because the preflight's motion check already gates that property.
S1 in two runs: every decisive beat is marked visible in the evidence, and watch_list_timing passes.

S4 in two runs: decisive_value_missing returns fit_to_deliver false with broken_property decisive_value_not_visible, and truncated_before_result returns result_not_in_reel, each with time_seconds within 0.5 s of the seeded time. Baseline S4 is the fail-before evidence. Where baseline S4 already met this, apply standing rule 1.

tasks.title: Gate the environment before capture
tasks.why: Recording the wrong environment is where private data enters a reel.
acceptance: Main instructions require an environment that is local or a test instance, shows no production indicators such as banners, production domains, or realistic customer records, and is signed in with a test or demo account.
